expectations.text: States the IPO transition correctly: the first annual report may omit 404(a) and 404(b); management's first 404(a) ICFR assessment is required in the SECOND Form 10-K; §302/§906 certifications apply immediately
expectations.evidence: States first 404(a) assessment lands in FIRST 10-K: "your first management 404(a) ICFR assessment lands in your first 10-K (FY2026, filed roughly Q1 2027)" — ground truth is the SECOND 10-K

expectations.text: Applies filer logic: $450M float + $180M revenue makes the company an accelerated filer under current thresholds ($75M-$700M float and ≥$100M revenue), so 404(b) auditor attestation applies once transition accommodations and any EGC status end
expectations.evidence: Only hedges "you may still be in 'accelerated filer' territory ($75M-$700M float)" and omits the ≥$100M revenue prong; asserts "Float, not revenue, drives" filer status

expectations.text: Checks EGC status: with revenue under $1.235B the company is likely an EGC (JOBS Act §103) and exempt from 404(b) for up to 5 years post-IPO unless disqualified earlier
expectations.evidence: "EGC (generally under $1.235B in annual revenue...)"; "exempt from the 404(b) auditor attestation requirement for up to five years post-IPO"

expectations.text: Flags the pending May 19, 2026 SEC proposal (large accelerated at $2B float; all non-accelerated exempt from 404(b); ~5-year on-ramp) as NOT FINAL — current thresholds remain operative law
expectations.evidence: No mention of the May 19, 2026 SEC filer-framework proposal anywhere in the response

expectations.text: Recommends starting ITGC design in year one anyway (scoping, access/change controls), since remediation windows and auditor reliance need operating history
expectations.evidence: "expect you to be functionally SOX-ready (documented controls, testing, remediation tracking) well before attestation is legally required — waiting... is a common and expensive mistake"
